meta.title: Sergeant Clarence Cole
meta.subtitle: Battery C, 153rd Field Artillery Battalion — European Theater of Operations, 1944–1945
meta.note: The service record, the Bronze Star citation, Special Orders 66 and the battalion morning reports agree on every date where they overlap. All 284 frames of the morning reports are transcribed. What remains is verification: no card has been read a second time, and the September order is still a first pass.

transcription.note: All 284 frames are transcribed. What remains is verification: 271 morning-report frames and 6 order frames have not been through a second reading.

subject.name: Clarence J. Cole
subject.mos: Squad Leader (653) on the discharge; 845 on the morning report of 5 September 1945
subject.weaponsQualification: Carbine, .30 cal — Sharpshooter; TSMG — 1st Class Gunner

enlistmentCard.film: Army Serial Number Electronic File, roll 1034, frame 5.96.
fields: Branch Immaterial (BI 00) — a selectee not yet assigned to an arm
Code 882. The code list NARA publishes with the file does not run to it.

decorations.name: European–African–Middle Eastern Campaign Medal
decorations.note: With five bronze service stars, one for each campaign credit.

commanders.name: Robert B. Ford
commanders.note: Signs the Battery C morning reports from the New York embarkation through to the occupation. Relieved and departed on the card of 26 June 1945.

commanders.name: Charles R. Wood Jr.
commanders.note: Signs the cards in the fortnight between Ford leaving and Kerkhoff arriving. Himself transferred to the 268th FA Bn on 11 July 1945.

commanders.name: Gordon F. Kerkhoff
commanders.note: Assigned and joined from Headquarters, 153rd FA Bn on 6 July 1945 and signs the battery cards from then on, including the two that name Sergeant Cole.

attachments.label: In combat, the Ardennes
attachments.note: This is where the battalion stood on 1 January 1945. Non-divisional artillery battalions moved between groups and corps often, so it does not describe the whole war.

attachments.label: In occupation, Germany
attachments.note: The battery's leave and furlough orders that month were issued by Headquarters, 32nd Field Artillery Brigade, which places Battery C under that brigade for administration. No order on file states the attachment directly.

pending: The calibre, stated rather than inferred
Attachments on dates other than 1 January 1945 and 20 August 1945

weapon.reading: Tractor-drawn heavy artillery — 155mm or 8-inch, not the truck-drawn 105mm.
evidence: The battery moves on tracked prime movers: two were wrecked on the night march to Tohogne, 27 December 1944 (frame 110).
It carries the MOS 244 Tractor Driver as a standing duty assignment (frames 78, 133).
Gun tubes were replaced after roughly 780 service rounds per gun — guns numbered 51 and 52 (frame 128).
It is non-divisional artillery, held at First Army and lent to divisions, which in 1944-45 means corps-level medium or heavy pieces.
weapon.caveat: No morning report states the calibre. All 284 frames have been read and none names a gun. This is an inference from how the battery moved and was maintained, not a documented fact, and should not be cited as one. The battalion's own unit history, FABN-153-0.1 at the National Archives at College Park, would settle it.

sources.note: Family papers. Confirms the sailing date independently of the morning reports.

sources.title: Army enlistment card, Clarence J. Cole
sources.citation: WD AGO Form 372. Electronic Army Serial Number Merged File, ca. 1938–1946, NARA ID 1263923, Record Group 64. Roll 1034, frame 5.96.
sources.note: One punch card per man entering the Army, filmed on 1,586 rolls and converted to a data file of 9,200,232 records. The card is a machine reading of a punch card, not the card itself; NARA compared 377 records against the originals and found errors in 5 serial numbers and 18 names.

sources.title: Citation — Award of Bronze Star Medal
sources.citation: War Department citation, Sergeant Clarence J. Cole, 36106875, Battery C, 153d Field Artillery Battalion.
sources.note: Family papers. An embossed War Department seal is struck at the foot; the headquarters named around its ring is only partly legible.

sources.title: Morning report, Battery C, 20 August 1945
sources.citation: WD AGO Form No. 1, Battery C, 153rd FA Bn, period ending 2400 hours, 20 August 1945. Signed Gordon F. Kerkhoff, Captain, FA.
sources.note: Supplied as a single image. Its frame number within the microfilm run has not been identified. This is the first card found that names Sergeant Cole.

sources.title: Morning report, Battery C, 25 August 1945
sources.citation: WD AGO Form No. 1, Battery C, 153rd FA Bn, period ending 2400 hours, 25 August 1945. Signed Gordon F. Kerkhoff, Captain, FA.

sources.title: Special Orders 66, Hq 153rd Field Artillery Battalion
sources.citation: Headquarters, 153rd Field Artillery Battalion, APO 758, 24 August 1945. Microfilm frames 248–252. By order of the Commanding Officer; Donald Kerr, Major, F.A., Adjutant.
sources.note: Transfers 142 named officers and enlisted men to the 70th Infantry Division. The nearest thing in the film to a battalion roster, and the source of the network diagram.

sources.title: Allied Army order of battle, Battle of the Bulge, 1 January 1945
sources.citation: Combined Arms Research Library digital collections, US Army Command and General Staff College, item p15040coll6/4713.
sources.note: A compiled order of battle rather than a unit record. Good enough to place the battalion on one date; not a substitute for the battalion's own after-action reports.

sources.title: ERA5 reanalysis weather, via the Open-Meteo Historical Weather API
sources.citation: ECMWF ERA5 global reanalysis, approximately 25 km grid, retrieved through archive-api.open-meteo.com. Open-Meteo data under CC BY 4.0; ERA5 under the Copernicus licence.
sources.note: Not a record of the war. A modern weather model rerun over the sparse observations that survive from the 1940s, reported for a grid cell up to 16 km from the village the clerk named. No morning-report card records the weather, so nothing here corroborates or is corroborated by the film. It is marked modelled everywhere it appears.

documents.title: The award
documents.caption: A general officer pins the Bronze Star. The battalion stands in formation behind him, in a damaged town. The family identifies the soldier as Sergeant Cole. Neither the date nor the place is written on the print.
documents.alt: A general officer in a steel helmet pins a medal to the field jacket of a soldier standing at attention, with ranks of helmeted soldiers and an American flag behind them in a damaged European town.

documents.title: Bronze Star citation
documents.caption: The typed citation, with the War Department seal embossed at the foot.
documents.alt: A typed citation on aged paper headed CITATION, AWARD OF BRONZE STAR MEDAL, with an embossed War Department seal near the bottom.

documents.title: Morning report, 20 August 1945
documents.caption: The first card found that names him. The first entry reads: Cole Clarence J, 36106875, Sgt, from duty to temporary duty at Treebeek, Holland. Five days' leave, four months after the war ended.
documents.alt: A typed US Army morning report card for Battery C, 153rd FA Bn, dated 20 August 1945, listing Sergeant Clarence J. Cole and three other enlisted men going on temporary duty.

documents.title: Morning report, 25 August 1945
documents.caption: Five days later his entry reads “Fr TD to dy” — returned from temporary duty. The card names the map sheet in use, Marburg 1/100,000 Sheet R-3, and counts three officers and sixty-seven men on the rolls.
documents.alt: A typed US Army morning report card for Battery C dated 25 August 1945, with a single entry for Sergeant Clarence J. Cole returning from temporary duty.

documents.title: Enlisted Record and Report of Separation
documents.caption: WD AGO Form 53-55, 22 October 1945. Fifty-seven numbered boxes covering three years of service.
documents.alt: A completed United States Army discharge form, Enlisted Record and Report of Separation, densely filled in with typewriting.

events.title: Born at Caro, Michigan
events.summary: He was thirty-seven years old when he sailed, and a farmer by trade.

events.title: Called to active service
events.summary: Enters active service at Fort Sheridan, Illinois, after a year on the inactive rolls of the Enlisted Reserve Corps.
events.verbatim: Inactive service ERC from 26 Nov 41 to 26 Nov 42.

events.title: Boards the transport at the New York Port of Embarkation
events.summary: Battery C leaves Fort Slocum by harbor boat and boards an Army transport at Terminal Pier before midnight.
events.verbatim: Boarded harbor boat at Ft Slocum NY at 1830 hrs. Arrived at Terminal Pier NYPE. Boarded Army Transport at 2315 hrs.
events.uncertainNote: The departure time is read as 1830 by one transcription of frame 1 and 1930 by the other. The digit is genuinely ambiguous on the microfilm and has not been resolved. Everything else on the card agrees.

events.title: Sails for Europe
events.summary: The transport clears the New York Port of Embarkation at 0630. The morning report does not name the destination; the discharge, written eighteen months later, records it as England.
events.verbatim: Army Transport left NYPE for destination at 0630 hrs.

events.title: Private Chmielewski to the ship's hospital
events.summary: Chester S. Chmielewski, 35761991, is carried from duty to the ship's hospital mid-ocean — the first personnel change recorded since the battery left New York. He was still with Battery C fifteen months later, a Pfc by then, leaving on furlough for Lyons the same week Cole went to Holland.
events.verbatim: Chmielewski, Pvt — Fr dy to hosp LD ship hosp.

corroboration.note: Full name and serial number read from the August 1945 card, which lists him again.

events.title: Routine transport duties
events.summary: A second man goes to the ship's hospital. Otherwise the battery is standing watches and drills at sea.
events.verbatim: Org performing routine transport duties.

events.title: Arrives in England
events.summary: Twelve days out of New York. The port is not recorded on the discharge, and the morning report for the day has not yet been read.
events.verbatim: Arrived at Port of Debarkation 1520 hrs.

events.title: Moves to Branksome
events.verbatim: Unit debarked fr Army Transport at 0400 hrs. Boarded train for destination. Unit arrived at Bournemouth (Branksome-Mount) Dorset U-4910 at 1130 hrs.

events.title: Alerted for departure
events.verbatim: ALERTED FOR DEPARTURE.

events.verbatim: ALERTED FOR DEPARTURE.

events.summary: The battery moved 23 miles to a new position.
events.verbatim: Left Branksome-Hants 0950 hours. Arrived at marshalling area C-14 at 1430 hours, distance traveled 23 miles.

events.title: Moves to Aboard LCT
events.summary: The battery moved 9 miles to a new position.
events.verbatim: Left marshalling area C-14 at 0930 hours. Arrived Southampton Dock S-4 at 1120 hours, distance traveled 9 miles. Loading of men and equipment on LCT craft completed at 2320 hours. Loaded at Hard S-4 Dock.

events.title: In support of active combat operations
events.summary: The Bronze Star citation dates his cited service from this day — three weeks after the Normandy landings — which places the battery on the Continent, or about to be, by the end of June.
events.verbatim: For meritorious service in support of active combat operations from 30 June 1944 to 15 March 1945 in France, Germany and Belgium.

events.title: Lands over Omaha Beach
events.summary: Twenty-four days after D-Day, and eight weeks after leaving New York, the battery came ashore in France.
events.verbatim: Arrived at Omaha Beach 1230 hours. Debarked and moved to vehicle transit area North Section at 2230 hours.
events.note: The Bronze Star cited period opens on this date. The citation and the morning report describe the same day from opposite ends: one says what it was for, the other says what happened.

events.title: Five days' leave in Holland
events.locationText: Herzhausen, Germany — map reference wG8188, Nord de Guerre grid
events.summary: The first morning report found that names him. The battery is in occupied Germany; Cole leaves on 19 August for five days at Treebeek, in Dutch Limburg, on a leave order from the 32nd Field Artillery Brigade. Three of his battery mates go to Lyons the same day, one of them Chmielewski, who had been carried to the ship's hospital crossing the Atlantic fifteen months before.
events.verbatim: Cole Clarence J 36106875 Sgt — Fr dy to TD Treebek, Holland per ltr Hq 32nd FA Brig (Lv Fur & Passes) dtd 16 Aug 45. Departed. Approx duration 5 days, as of 19 Aug 45.

events.title: Special Orders 66 — a hundred and forty-two men sent home

context.title: D-Day
context.summary: Allied forces land on five Normandy beaches. Cole had been in England three weeks.

context.title: Operation Cobra
context.summary: The breakout from the Normandy hedgerows begins with a saturation bombing west of Saint-Lô.

context.title: Paris is liberated
context.summary: The German garrison surrenders and the pursuit across France accelerates beyond its own supply lines.

context.title: The Ardennes offensive begins
context.summary: Three German armies attack through the Ardennes in winter fog, opening the Battle of the Bulge. Cole's campaign credits include Ardennes, and his citation names Belgium.

context.title: The Rhine is crossed at Remagen
context.summary: The Ludendorff Bridge is captured intact and the last natural barrier into Germany falls.

context.title: V-E Day
context.summary: Germany's unconditional surrender takes effect and the war in Europe ends. Cole would sail for home five months later.

crossReferences.detail: The discharge and the morning report of 3 May 1944 (frame 1) both give 3 May 1944. Produced eighteen months apart by different clerks.

crossReferences.claim: Bronze Star cited period opens on the landing
crossReferences.detail: The citation runs from 30 June 1944. The morning report for that day (frame 17) records the battery arriving at Omaha Beach at 1230 hours and moving to the vehicle transit area at 2230. The cited period begins on the day the battery first set foot in France.

crossReferences.claim: Bronze Star cited period closes on the Rhine crossing
crossReferences.detail: The citation runs to 15 March 1945. The morning report for that day (frame 151) records a 40-mile move into the Remagen bridgehead on the east bank of the Rhine. The cited period brackets the battery combat record from the landing to the crossing of the Rhine.

The order of battle places the battalion under XVIII Airborne Corps on 1 January 1945. The morning report for that day (frame 113) puts Battery C at Werbomont, on the northern shoulder of the Bulge, which is consistent with that corps sector.

crossReferences.claim: Eighteen men of Special Orders 66 are placed in Battery C
crossReferences.detail: Special Orders 66 carries no battery column, so it cannot place a man in Battery C on its own. Cross-matching its serial numbers against the Battery C morning reports resolves eighteen of the 142: thirteen on an exact serial match and five where the two transcriptions differ by one or two digits.

Not present in frames 1-218. No award of any kind is recorded in the transcribed cards. If the battalion announced it in the morning reports it will be in frames 219-284, which cover the period the award was most likely published.
